name: Villa de Leyva
tagline: A whitewashed 16th-century colonial town on one of the largest cobbled squares in the Americas, with fossils, waterfalls and desert-like hills.
highlight: Standing in the vast Plaza Mayor, a cobbled square the size of several football pitches, with the town's white walls and red roofs around it.
shortDescription: A perfectly preserved colonial town three hours from Bogotá, with the huge Plaza Mayor, whitewashed streets, Iguaque hikes, waterfalls, fossils and wineries.
metaDescription: A Villa de Leyva travel guide: the Plaza Mayor, colonial streets, Pozos Azules, El Fósil, Iguaque, Ráquira, how to get there from Bogotá, where to stay and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Bogotá El Dorado (BOG), about 3.5–4 hours by road
knownFor: Colonial architecture, Plaza Mayor, fossils, day trips
goodFor: Weekend trips, history, cycling, slow travel

image.alt: The vast cobbled Plaza Mayor of Villa de Leyva with its white church

intro: Villa de Leyva was founded in 1572, and it has been preserved as a national monument since 1954, so building styles, roof tiles and whitewash follow the colonial pattern. It sits at 2,150 metres in a high, dry valley in Boyacá, with a mild, sunny climate that contrasts with cloudy Bogotá.

The heart of the town is the Plaza Mayor, one of the largest cobbled plazas in the Americas at around 14,000 square metres, surrounded by whitewashed buildings and a church. Narrow streets lead off in a grid, past courtyards, museums and cafés. Weekends fill with visitors from Bogotá, but weekdays are quiet.

The surroundings offer plenty to do. There are fossils of a 110-million-year-old kronosaurus at El Fósil, blue pools called Pozos Azules, the Iguaque sanctuary with a sacred lake, waterfalls, wineries and the pottery village of Ráquira. Cycling is popular. It is about three to four hours by bus from Bogotá, and two days is a good stay.

whyVisit.intro: Villa de Leyva is the prettiest colonial town within reach of Bogotá.
